description: v1.2 signed-int32 two-backend slice (ISSUE-0397 I6 part 3). The JS-divergent int32 matrix: per-case backends lists and no three-backend sidecar contract — the JS lane executes none of these cases in this epic (the uniform three-backend sidecar schema pins one shared expectation per fixture, and the JS lane's legacy safe-range gate produces no E8004 for the in-legacy-range cases below; js-v12-int32-bytes owns the later promotion of this matrix into uniform sidecars). Every case runs the real frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) under the per-case A5 invocation (COMMON_SHADOW + DEAL_V1_2_INT32 — none of these cases is catalogued) → real LuaBackend/JvmBackend codegen → luajit / javac + java executing the emitted artifact. The matrix re-homes the removed backend-runtime int-add-overflow fixture as int32-add-overflow (the re-home whose retained-route coverage the A5 profile-selection merge moved out of the uniform-sidecar population); the other cases are the additive signed32 replacements for the catalogued safe-int-era families: sub/mul/neg/div/conversion overflow, the literal boundaries, the both-raise precedence parity, the table-read int boundary, the std/math.absInt(MIN_VALUE) gate, the async completion int boundary, the standalone overflow expression, the number-pow IEEE band (the pinned IEEE-754 special-case table), and the JVM-only declared host int return boundary (the LuaJIT host-boundary replacement is test_runtime_int32.lua and the fixed corpus).

tests.name: int32-add-overflow
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: 2147483647 + 1 leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes (the re-home of the removed backend-runtime int-add-overflow fixture; LuaJIT is the reference)

tests.name: int32-sub-overflow
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: -2147483648 - 1 leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes

tests.name: int32-mul-overflow
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: 2147483647 * 2 leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes

tests.name: int32-neg-min
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: unary minus on the minimum value routes through the checked negation gate — -(-2147483648) leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes

tests.name: int32-div-min-neg-one
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: -2147483648 / -1 computes 2147483648, which leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes (the truncated-division overflow)

tests.name: int32-convert-range
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int: int(2147483648.0) — an integral number at 2^31 — leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes (the conversion gate)

tests.name: int32-literal-boundaries
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int literals: the maximum 2147483647 and the minimum -2147483648 (the immediate-token unary-minus form) compile, run, and hold their exact values on both retained routes (TEST_FAIL-asserted)

tests.name: int32-array-precedence-parity
tests.description: v1.2 cross-backend parity for the both-raise error precedence: (2147483647 + 1) === xs[-1] — both operands can raise, and the left operand's checked int32 arithmetic must raise E8004 first, never the right read's E8002, on both retained routes

tests.name: int32-table-read-boundary
tests.description: v1.2 signed 32-bit int boundary: a table read holding the integral number 2147483648.0 assigned to an int | null binding crosses the typed boundary and raises E8004 on both retained routes (the int boundary gate)

tests.name: int32-math-abs-min
tests.description: v1.2 std/math: absInt(-2147483648) computes the magnitude 2147483648, which leaves the signed 32-bit range and raises E8004 on both retained routes (the absInt arm computes the long magnitude before the gate — LuaJIT is the reference)

tests.name: int32-async-completion-safe
tests.description: v1.2 async completion int boundary: an async export completing with the maximal signed 32-bit int 2147483647 passes the await-site completion check and the run completes (runtime-ok) on both retained routes
tests.source:
async function big(): int { return 2147483647; }
export async function test(): int { return await big(); }

tests.name: int32-standalone-overflow
tests.description: v1.2 standalone expression statement: the discarded 2147483647 + 1 still evaluates through the checked int32 arithmetic and raises E8004 on both retained routes (evaluation is real, matching LuaJIT)

tests.name: int32-number-pow-ieee
tests.description: v1.2 number ** IEEE-754 band on both retained routes: exact powers, 0.0 ** 0.0 === 1.0, 0.0 ** -1.0 === +Infinity, the negative-base fractional NaN (self-unequal), pow(1, NaN) === 1.0, pow(NaN, 0) === 1.0, pow(-1, +Infinity) === 1.0, overflow to +Infinity, and underflow to +0 (TEST_FAIL-asserted; LuaJIT C pow and the JVM pinned numPow wrapper agree on every case)

tests.name: int32-host-int-return
tests.description: v1.2 declared host int return boundary: a host function returning the long 2147483648 through a declared int return crosses the typed boundary and raises E8004 (the JVM host-ABI slice surface is JVM-only; the LuaJIT host-boundary replacement is test_runtime_int32.lua and the fixed corpus)
